The Admissions Officer
Cabrini Hopetoun Rehabilitation
2-6 Hopetoun Street
Elsternwick

24/07/2018

Dear Doctor,
Re: Mr. Julian McDonald, DOB: 12/01/1950

Thank you for seeing Mr. McDonald, who is being transferred today following total knee
replacement surgery. His condition would require your care. [Avoid ultrashort sentence]

On 20/07/2018, Mr. McDonald was admitted to the Alfred Hospital for surgery on his left knee.
Following the operation, he reported pain which impaired his mobility. The pain has improved on
ketamine, and he is currently on paracetamol, ibuprofen, targin and oxycodone. Additionally, he           Commented [DSM1]: Targin: trade name
experienced mild agitation and insomnia, together with significant somnolence and snoring,
despite inadequate analgesia.

Mr. McDonald has hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, along with osteoarthritis and gout, which
are managed accordingly. His BMI is 35, and he smokes 20 cigarettes and drinks six to ten times           Commented [DSM2]: was: BMI is a sign not a fact
daily. Kindly note that he lives in a caravan and has had penicillin allergic rash when he was a child.   Commented [DSM3]: penicillin-allergic

In light of the above, Mr. McDonald would require physiotherapy and occupational therapy home
visit to assess the suitability of returning to live in the caravan. He is due to have his stitches
removed in ten days and an appointment is arranged on 07/09/2018 with Dr. B Mossley, who
performed the surgery. Sleep studies, social work, as well as alcohol and drug input, would also be
appreciated.

Thank you for taking care of Mr. McDonald. Should there be any queries please do not hesitate to
contact me.

Yours faithfully,
Doctor
